source: GPT-f: Polu & Sutskever (2020) Generative language modeling for automated theorem proving
finding: Transformer proposes next proof step in Metamath, best-first search picks which to expand. A learned value function trained on its own search outcomes helped. More attempts per theorem helped with diminishing returns. New short proofs were accepted into the Metamath library.
numbers: Held-out Metamath: 56.22% vs 21.16% prior SOTA (MetaGen-IL). Policy+value iteration 2 at a=1: 47.21% (+4.6 over policy only). Attempts a=2 42.90%, 4 47.29, 8 51.26, 16 54.05, 32 56.50 (d=256).
quote: closing 56.22% of proofs from a held-out test set (vs 21.16% for the current state of the art
limits: Metamath is a simple formal system; adding synthetic proofs at 5% of data hurt. Gain per doubling of attempts shrinks (+4.39, +3.97, +2.99, +2.45).
agent_relevance: Founding case of model suggests, search chooses. Verifier-checked steps plus a value estimate beat a single pass. Doubling attempts has predictable shrinking returns: cap the budget in S3/S4.

source: Han et al. (2021) PACT: Proof Artifact Co-Training for theorem proving with language models
finding: Training the tactic model also on auxiliary tasks mined from proof terms (next lemma, type prediction) raised Lean success. Web-math pretraining also helped.
numbers: Held-out mathlib theorems: 32% to 48% with PACT. 37% on a separate out-of-distribution test suite (abstract text).
quote: improves theorem proving success rate on a held-out suite of test theorems from 32% to 48%
limits: Lean 3 mathlib only; gains come from training data design, which our scaffold cannot change.
agent_relevance: Training-only lever. The prompt-side analogue is giving the model proof-state context and nearby lemma names.

source: Lample et al. (2022) HyperTree Proof Search (HTPS)
finding: MCTS-style search over proof hypergraphs with a critic and online training on its own search results. Online training was critical.
numbers: Metamath held-out: 65.4% with HTPS alone (prior 56.5% GPT-f), 82.6% with online training. Lean miniF2F-curriculum 31% to 42%. miniF2F-test 41% pass@64 vs 36.6% GPT-f. 58.6% on miniF2F-valid (intro text).
quote: with HTPS alone, a model trained on annotated proofs manages to prove 65.4%
limits: Heavy compute for online training. Hypergraph needed because tactics split into subgoals (AND-nodes).
agent_relevance: Track subgoals as AND-nodes: a split tactic needs all children closed, and one dead child kills the branch (S4 decomposition).

source: Jiang et al. (2022) Thor: Wielding hammers to integrate language models and automated theorem provers
finding: The model chooses when to call the symbolic hammer (Sledgehammer) for premise search. The hybrid beat either alone.
numbers: PISA: 39.0% (LM alone) to 57.0% (Thor). 8.2% of problems solved by neither LM nor Sledgehammer alone. miniF2F 29.6% to 29.9% with much less compute. LM premise-selection steps advance the proof only 1.9% of the time vs 28.2% for steps with no premises.
quote: increases a language model's success rate on the PISA dataset from 39% to 57%
limits: Isabelle only; gain depends on a strong hammer.
agent_relevance: Models are poor at premise recall (1.9% step success): route recall to a retrieval or solver tool and keep the model for structure.

source: Jiang et al. (2022) Draft, Sketch, and Prove (DSP)
finding: LLM drafts an informal proof, maps it to a formal sketch with open gaps, an off-the-shelf prover fills the gaps. Plan-first lifted success a lot over the same prover alone.
numbers: miniF2F-test: baseline 20.9% to 39.3%; human informal proof 38.9% test, 42.6% valid; Codex informal 40.6% valid. Minerva drafter on test: 8B 36.5%, 62B 34.0%, 540B 30.3% (-2.8, -5.3, -9.0 vs human draft).
limits: Bigger drafter was worse on test; Isabelle; 244 test problems, so small gaps are noisy.
agent_relevance: Supports plan then fill gaps (S3 plan, S4 per-gap search). A stronger drafter did not help; the gap-filling check is what counts.

source: Yang et al. (2023) LeanDojo: retrieval-augmented provers (ReProver)
finding: Premise retrieval helped. Random splits overstate skill because similar theorems leak; a split needing unseen premises is much harder. GPT-4 zero-shot was weak.
numbers: LeanDojo test Pass@1, random split: ReProver 51.2%, no retrieval 47.6, GPT-4 29.0, tidy 23.8. novel_premises split: 26.3, 23.2, 7.4, 5.3. MiniF2F 26.5%, ProofNet 13.8%.
quote: Splitting theorems randomly can overestimate the prover's performance
limits: GPT-4 may have seen the proofs (contamination) yet did worst. Trained 5 days on one GPU.
agent_relevance: Success roughly halves when the needed lemma was unseen. Give the agent retrieval, not memory.

source: Xin et al. (2024) DeepSeek-Prover V1
finding: 8 million synthetic statement-proof pairs from auto-formalized problems, filtered by the verifier, trained a 7B whole-proof model.
numbers: Lean 4 miniF2F-test: 46.3% with 64 samples, 52% cumulative; GPT-4 23.0% at 64 samples; tree-search RL baseline 41.0%. FIMO: 5 of 148 vs GPT-4 0.
limits: Statement-quality filtering was key; sampling with no search.
agent_relevance: Many cheap verified samples beat a stronger general model on the same budget; fits best-of-N with a hard checker.

source: Xin et al. (2024) DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5 (RLPAF, RMaxTS)
finding: RL from proof assistant feedback plus a Monte-Carlo tree search that truncates a failed proof at the last good tactic and resumes. CoT and plain modes complement each other.
numbers: miniF2F-test 63.5% (CoT+non-CoT mixture with RMaxTS), ProofNet 25.3%. Table 3: SFT single-pass about 54.7-56.3% vs RL 56.5-59.6%; RL+CoT+RMaxTS 62.7% (+3.7 over SFT). Plain UCT with no intrinsic reward fell to non-search level.
limits: CoT advantage grows with sample budget; search gains are orthogonal to RL gains. Run-to-run spread 0.3 to 0.8 points.
agent_relevance: Truncate-and-resume: keep the verified prefix, rewrite only from the first failing step (G2). Two prompt modes gave complementary solves.

source: Ren et al. (2025) DeepSeek-Prover-V2 (subgoal decomposition RL)
finding: A big general model decomposes a problem into lemma subgoals with sorry placeholders; a 7B prover solves each; the stitched proof seeds RL.
numbers: miniF2F-test 82.4% at pass@32, 88.9% at pass@8192. PutnamBench 47 of 658. ProverBench AIME 24-25: prover solves some of 15; informal DeepSeek-V3 majority vote solves 8 of 15, so the formal-informal gap is narrowing.
limits: 671B model; 7B weaker. Still far from solving most of Putnam.
agent_relevance: Decompose with a strong model, solve leaves with a cheap model plus the checker: the S3 plan / S4 leaf split.

source: Lin et al. (2025) Goedel-Prover
finding: 1.64M autoformalized statements and expert iteration across successive provers; SFT alone beat the prior RL-trained model.
numbers: miniF2F Pass@32 57.6% (+7.6 over DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5-RL); PutnamBench 7 solved at Pass@512 (first reported 8, one withdrawn after author discussion); 800K+ statements solved.
limits: One claimed Putnam solve was withdrawn after checking.
agent_relevance: Expert iteration needs a trusted verifier, and claimed results need external audit.

source: Dong & Ma (2025) STP: Self-play Theorem Prover
finding: One model plays conjecturer and prover; proved conjectures become training data. Fixes the waste where most sampling compute yields no proof.
numbers: LeanWorkbook proved 28.5% vs 13.2% prior best. miniF2F-test 65.0% pass@3200, ProofNet-test 23.9%, PutnamBench 8/644 at pass@3200. 3.6M generated conjectures.
quote: 98.5% of the compute yields no successful proofs
limits: Training method; compute heavy.
agent_relevance: Conjecture-then-prove fits S3 generating intermediate lemmas with the verifier as the only judge.

source: Xin et al. (2025) BFS-Prover
finding: Plain best-first search with length normalization and DPO on compiler feedback beat value-function and MCTS systems when scaled.
numbers: miniF2F-test 72.95%. Uses beam-search filtering of easy statements, length-normalized paths, no value function.
quote: challenges the perceived necessity of complex tree search methods
limits: Large budgets; simple search wins only when well scaled.
agent_relevance: Do not over-engineer S4 search; first scale a plain loop with a hard checker.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Kimina-Prover Preview
finding: RL for long thinking blocks aligned with Lean code gives strong results even at pass@1 and scales with budget.
numbers: miniF2F-test 80.7% at pass@8192.
limits: Preview model; the thinking format needs training.
agent_relevance: Informal reasoning aligned to formal steps, then verified, supports think-then-check.

source: Thakur et al. (2023) COPRA: in-context learning agent for formal theorem proving
finding: GPT-4 in a stateful backtracking agent: it proposes a tactic, the prover runs it, errors and search history are fed back, lemmas are retrieved. No fine-tuning. Beat few-shot GPT-4 and rivaled fine-tuned ReProver.
numbers: miniF2F-test pass@1: few-shot GPT-4 13.52%, GPT-3.5 2.8%, CodeLlama 0%; COPRA GPT-4 29.92%, GPT-3.5 9.02%, CodeLlama 5.73%; ReProver 25.00%; Llemma 25.8-26.2%. Few-shot GPT-4 with 60 attempts at T=0.7: 15.98%.
limits: Needs a strong base model. Table text garbled in extraction, so ablation rows (no backtracking, no retrieval, about 24.6 to 29.1%) are not pinned down.
agent_relevance: Closest published match to our agent: training-free LLM loop with verifier feedback, error history and backtracking; about 2x over one-shot with the same model.

source: First, Rabe, Ringer, Brun (2023) Baldur: whole-proof generation and repair with LLMs
finding: Whole proofs from a fine-tuned LLM beat step-by-step search; feeding the proof assistant error back to a repair model added more.
numbers: 6,336 Isabelle/HOL theorems: whole-proof 47.9% vs search-based 39.0%; repair adds 1.5%; added context adds more; +8.7% over Thor; Baldur plus Thor 65.7%.
quote: LLMs can repair proofs, including their own erroneous proof attempts
limits: Fine-tuned model; repair gain small alone.
agent_relevance: Supports G2: repair from the real checker message gives a reliable gain; combine with a complementary tool.

source: Zheng, Han, Polu (2021) miniF2F benchmark
finding: Cross-system benchmark of 488 olympiad and course problems for several proof systems, with GPT-f baselines.
numbers: 488 statements (244 valid, 244 test). Pass@N means N attempts per statement.
limits: Saturated by 2025 (Seed-Prover 99.6%).
agent_relevance: Use as a sanity test only; saturated benchmarks cannot separate scaffolds.

source: Tsoukalas et al. (2024) PutnamBench
finding: Hard multi-assistant benchmark of Putnam problems. Early LLM provers solved almost none.
numbers: Lean 640 problems: GPT-4 1, COPRA 1, ReProver 0. Isabelle 640: GPT-4 1, DSP 4, Sledgehammer 3. Coq 412: GPT-4 1, COPRA 1, Tactician 0, CoqHammer 0.
limits: Tiny counts, so differences are noisy.
agent_relevance: 2024 ceiling for training-free GPT-4 was about 1 in 640. Later gains (Seed-Prover 331/657) came from training plus refinement.

source: Song, Yang, Anandkumar (2024) Lean Copilot
finding: LLM tactic suggestion, proof search and premise selection integrated into Lean as a copilot.
numbers: Human assistance: 2.08 manual proof steps on average vs 3.86 for AESOP. Automation: 74.2% of steps vs 40.1% for AESOP (85% better).
limits: Selected textbook theorems only.
agent_relevance: Human-in-loop pattern: model suggests, rule-based search closes.

source: ByteDance Seed (2025) Seed-Prover: Deep and broad reasoning for automated theorem proving
finding: Lemma-style whole proofs refined iteratively on Lean compiler feedback, proved lemmas and self-summaries; light, medium, heavy inference tiers. Refinement beat raw Pass@k.
numbers: 78.1% of formalized past IMO problems; MiniF2F-test 99.6% (medium); PutnamBench 331/657 vs 86/657 for Goedel-Prover-V2; IMO 2025: 5 of 6. Light setting 8-16 refinements equals about Pass@64-256 sample budget; IMO 2022 P2 solved by light refinement but without refinement only at Pass@8192.
quote: iteratively refining proofs using Lean compiler feedback in conjunction with self-summarization can surpass the limits of single-pass
limits: Lean-specific; heavy setting runs for days; geometry needs a separate engine.
agent_relevance: Strongest evidence for a scaffold loop: refine on checker output, summarize, keep proved lemmas. One refinement run can beat a 30 to 100x larger sample budget.

source: DeepMind AlphaProof (2024; Nature 2025), as cited in DeepSeek-Prover-V2
finding: AlphaProof, an AlphaZero-style RL system with test-time RL on Lean, reached IMO silver-medal level in 2024. DeepSeek-Prover-V2 says its approach shares the test-time RL principle.
numbers: Not opened: only the citation in the V2 paper was read.
limits: The AlphaProof paper itself was not read this session.
agent_relevance: Read before designing test-time variant generation.

source: Synthesis: whole-proof vs stepwise search
finding: Baldur (47.9% whole-proof vs 39.0% search), DeepSeek-Prover V1 (46.3% vs 41.0% tree-search RL) and BFS-Prover (plain BFS 72.95%) show no single search style dominates; budget and verifier matter more.
numbers: See c15, c07, c12.
limits: Different datasets and budgets; not matched comparisons.
agent_relevance: Let the program pick breadth vs refinement by budget.

source: Synthesis: sample budget scaling
finding: Pass rate climbs roughly log-linearly with samples, then flattens: GPT-f a=2 to 32 gives 42.9 to 56.5; DeepSeek-V2 82.4 at 32 to 88.9 at 8192; Seed-Prover refinement replaces thousands of samples.
numbers: From c01, c09, c19.
limits: pass@k assumes independent samples; refinement breaks that.
agent_relevance: Spend budget on refinement from checker feedback first, sampling second (G2, G4).

source: Synthesis: contamination and leakage
finding: Random splits leak near-duplicate theorems (LeanDojo); Goedel-Prover withdrew one Putnam claim; miniF2F saturates at 99.6%.
numbers: ReProver random 51.2% vs novel_premises 26.3%.
limits: Contamination is hard to prove either way.
agent_relevance: Evaluate on fresh problems with a held-out check (G3).

source: Synthesis: model proposes, tool disposes
finding: Thor (premise-selection steps 1.9% effective), Lean Copilot (74.2% vs AESOP 40.1%) and DSP (prover fills sketch gaps) all show the hybrid beats either side.
numbers: See c04, c18, c05.
limits: Hybrid gains may shrink as models improve.
agent_relevance: Keep symbolic tools in the loop for premise search and closing easy goals.

source: Synthesis: base model strength gates training-free search
finding: Under the same COPRA loop GPT-4 gets 29.92%, GPT-3.5 9.02%, CodeLlama 5.73%; few-shot GPT-4 gets 13.52%.
numbers: Loop gain about 2.2x at GPT-4; 60 sampled attempts only 15.98%.
limits: Single benchmark, single prompt design.
agent_relevance: Scaffold gain multiplies base ability; expect little on weak models.

source: Synthesis: when plain search beats fancy search
finding: In V1.5, MCTS without intrinsic reward (plain UCT) fell to non-search level, while BFS-Prover reached 72.95% with plain best-first search and no value function. Search choice matters less than a good exploration signal and scale.
numbers: V1.5 RMaxTS vs single pass at 16x6400: about +1 to +4 points depending on mode; BFS 72.95% miniF2F-test.
limits: Different base models and budgets.
agent_relevance: Pick the simplest search that keeps diversity; verify gains per budget.
